Badges Promoted, Certified, Master data; any item except dashboards can be promoted (by users with write permission) or certified; only admin-specified users certify or label master data; master data only for data items; must be enabled by a Fabric admin.

concept_html:
A tenant with 400 workspaces needs two things before anyone trusts its data: a way to find data by business area, and a way to tell the authoritative copy from the rest. Fabric gives you domains and endorsement. Microsoft Learn shows neither with a preview label (checked September 2026).

Domains group workspaces by business area, such as Finance or Marketing. You can split a domain into subdomains.

  • You associate workspaces with a domain. Every item in the workspace inherits the domain.
  • Users filter the OneLake catalog by domain to find relevant data.
  • Some tenant settings can be delegated to domain level, so each area sets its own rules.
  • Domain assignment does not grant or restrict access. Workspace roles and item permissions decide who sees what.

Three roles manage domains. Fabric admins create domains and name domain admins. Domain admins, ideally the business owners, edit their domain and associate workspaces. Domain contributors are workspace admins allowed to assign their own workspaces to the domain.

Endorsement labels an item with one of three badges:

Badge Meaning Who applies it
Promoted The creators think it is ready to share Anyone with write access to the item
Certified An authorised reviewer confirms it meets the organisation's standards Only users a Fabric admin names
Master data The authoritative source for core data such as customer lists Only users a Fabric admin names

Any item except a Power BI dashboard can be promoted or certified. Master data applies only to items that hold data, such as lakehouses and semantic models. Certification and master data work only after a Fabric admin enables them.

Endorsed items get a badge and appear first in some lists. That helps people pick the right copy. It does not stop anyone using an uncertified one.

title: Domains and endorsement, finding the right data
why_html: A company had five semantic models called "Sales" across four workspaces. Two finance directors presented different quarterly revenue to the board. Both had used a model called "Sales". Certifying one model, retiring the others, and filing the finance workspaces under a Finance domain made the right model the first result anyone found.
